name: Würzburg Residence with the Court Gardens and Residence Square
description: The Würzburg Residence is an 18th-century Baroque palace in Würzburg, Germany, built for the city's powerful prince-bishops between 1720 and 1744. Its grand staircase is crowned by a vast ceiling fresco by Giovanni Battista Tiepolo, and lavish halls and a chapel lie beyond it. Napoleon reportedly called it Europe's "largest parsonage." Formal gardens surround it, and bombing in World War II left it damaged, so restoration continues today.
